name: DeepSeek Chat

selectors._sendButtonNote: Empty on purpose: prompts are sent with Enter, which carried every live build. The old value matched only a <button> and DeepSeek's send control is a div, so it never matched and every prompt logged "No send button found". That control is also the stop control and is told apart only by hashed classes (_stopButtonNote), so there is no stable selector to give it.
selectors._citationNote: Smart Search's source badges: -15, read as "-15" mid-sentence. Seen in DeepSeek's own replies, 2026-10-01.
selectors._thinkingNote:
MEASURED 8 October 2026. With DeepThink on, a turn is
holding a header span "Thought for 1 second", then
reasoning
, then
answer
. The reasoning is a ds-markdown too, so assistantMessage is read with it excluded. Clicking the header collapses the reasoning by REMOVING .ds-think-content from the page, not hiding it, so a collapsed one is expanded before it is read. The prompt you sent is a .ds-message as well, with no reasoning in it.
selectors._copyButtonNote: Matches the code-block toolbar buttons; the caller filters by the label so Download is not clicked. .code-info-button-text is the only unhashed class on that control - the rest (ds-button--capsule etc.) are design-system modifiers and the surrounding path is entirely build hashes.
selectors._assistantNote: ds-markdown first: it is the container DeepSeek renders assistant content into. The previous value led with [data-testid] and [class*=message][class*=assistant], which matched three nodes that never update while a reply streams - a build step sat at messages=3, chars=9019 for the full 300s wait because the node being watched was the PREVIOUS answer.
selectors._streamNote: MEASURED on 11 August 2026 by instrumenting a real reply: DeepSeek streams its answer over POST /api/v0/chat/completion with content-type text/event-stream. Exact rather than a loose pattern on purpose - the earlier guess also matched chat_session/create, and a short request that opened AND closed before the reply began would have satisfied 'all streams closed' and ended the wait early. The reply is never read from this; only its start and end are used. resume_stream MEASURED 8 October 2026: when the completion stream ends without its close event, the page itself POSTs /api/v0/chat/resume_stream at once and carries on the reply over it (application/json when the server has already finished, otherwise the rest of the reply). Unwatched, that looked like a closed stream: the wait could read a reply before the resume finished it, or call a reply dropped and send the prompt a second time while the page was still fetching it.
selectors._replySignalsNote: MEASURED 9 October 2026 from a captured /api/v0/chat/completion body. A reply ends with data: {"p":"response/status","o":"SET","v":"FINISHED"}; the statuses in DeepSeek's bundle are FINISHED, WIP, INCOMPLETE, CONTENT_FILTER, CONTEXT_LENGTH_EXCEEDED and TIMEOUT. Errors that replace a reply arrive as `event: hint` or `event: toast` with data {type, content, ...} inside a 200 stream. Inside the reply's own text these quotes are escaped, so the patterns cannot match what the model wrote. Read only once the stream has ended.

completionRules._maxWaitNote: Raised from 120s. A reasoning model on a plan- or build-sized prompt was still thinking when the old wait expired, so a partial response got extracted and then failed to parse. The wait ends as soon as the reply is complete, so a longer ceiling costs nothing on fast answers.
completionRules._stopButtonNote: DeepSeek has NO distinct stop control, measured 11 August 2026. The stop button IS the send button - one element that gains ds-button--disabled when idle - so 'enabled' means either 'generating' OR 'you have typed something', and the only distinguishing classes are hashed (_52c986b). A selector here would be both ambiguous and the kind of guess every serious bug in this project has come from. The reply stream above is a better end signal and is exact.

_controlsNote: DeepSeek has no model dropdown. Two inline toggles, each reporting its own state. The Instant/Advanced mode radiogroup this used to set is gone from the site (September 2026), so the Mode control was removed rather than left failing on every conversation open.

controls.label: Deep thinking
controls._defaultNote: Off by default. With DeepThink on, a build-sized prompt spent the whole 300s completion wait in its reasoning phase without starting to answer, so the step timed out and every step behind it blocked. Build steps want a fast structured answer, not a long deliberation. It is one click away in the rail for the cases that want it.

controlSelectors._note: toggle keys off aria-pressed rather than a class: setFlagByText reads that attribute anyway, and .ds-toggle-button stopped matching after a DeepSeek redesign. Confirmed live 2026-10-01 from DeepSeek's own message records: research turns went out with thinking and search on, agent turns with thinking off. If the toggles ever report unavailable, the run log prints the page's pressable controls to copy from.

_thinkingHeaderTextNote: Matched against the header span's whole text, case-insensitively. "Thinking" while the model reasons, then "Thought for N seconds" once it ends - both seen live 8 October 2026. An English-language UI is assumed, as deepThinkingText already does.
_contextBudgetNote: Roughly how much conversation this provider will hold before a build should continue in a new thread, in characters. A deliberately conservative guess - nothing can read the real window, and being wrong in this direction costs one seeded prompt while being wrong the other way loses a step fifteen deep. Counted from what we send and the replies we receive, never from the page.

_replyErrorsNote: What DeepSeek shows instead of a reply, MEASURED 9 October 2026 by injecting each fault into a real page (scripts/deepseek-faults.mjs). The texts are DeepSeek's own strings from its bundle (main.3c07bbc8f6.js), English and Chinese. A busy, server-error or rate-limit reply is a row in .ds-virtual-list-visible-items with no .ds-message, so the message count never moves; a reply cut short by a busy server keeps its partial .ds-markdown and adds a bar with the notice and a Continue button beside it. CONTEXT_LENGTH_EXCEEDED shows nothing but the partial answer, so it is read from the stream. Signed out (an invalid token, code 40003), the page goes to /sign_in. Busy is sent again after 5s, 20s and 60s, a rate limit once after 60s; a full conversation rolls over, and signed out stops with a 'sign in again' message.
